result.headline: Roll tracks large setpoint swings with a fixed lag; velocity and yaw estimates jump; low-voltage warning at 0.518 s.
result.explanation: The roll loop follows its setpoint with a fixed lag of about 0.981 s. The abnormal items are the ±44 deg setpoint swings and discontinuous velocity and yaw estimates. Their origin cannot be separated on this data.

evidence.quote: CHANGE control.attitude_setpoint[roll] at t=6.127 s: -43.66 -> 43.27 deg (step 86.93, 362.2x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: The roll setpoint itself swings by 86.93 deg in a short time, so the demand is abrupt.

evidence.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=0 to 1.32 s (peak |error| 63.625 deg)
evidence.shows: Tracking errors are mostly lag after setpoint steps. Correlation is 0.975 at a 0.981 s lag in 0-20 s and 0.973 in 30-60 s.

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.velocity[x] at t=13.001 s: 19.87 -> -9.52 m/s (step -29.39, 183.7x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: A velocity estimate jump with no matching airspeed change, which points to an estimator or sensor discontinuity.

evidence.quote: CHANGE vehicle.attitude[yaw] at t=12.479 s: 85.682 -> -27.449 deg (step -113.131, 190.7x its usual variation)
evidence.shows: A yaw estimate jump close in time to the velocity step at 13.001 s.

evidence.quote: EVENT t=0.518 s controller.event[mavros: Battery] mavros: Battery: WARN: Low voltage
evidence.shows: The only event in the recording. It is an early warning with no follow-on failsafe.

checked.check: Order of first departures from baseline in 0-20 s
checked.result: No signal left baseline before the single battery event.

checked.check: Roll setpoint vs roll attitude, 0-20 s and 30-60 s
checked.result: Correlation is 0.975 and 0.973 at a 0.981 s lag. Typical difference falls from 5.915 deg to 3.191 deg.
checked.about: Control loop, actuator or attitude sensor fault (indirect: observed at the attitude estimate)

checked.check: Actuator and throttle behaviour in 0-20 s
checked.result: ch[1] moves with roll, ch[2] sits at 1100 us until about t=13 s, and throttle is 0 % from 0.979 s to 12.361 s.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[roll] diverged from its setpoint from t=0 to 1.32 s (peak |error| 63.625 deg)
effects.why: This is lag behind the setpoint steps, not a loss of control authority.

effects.quote: TRACKING vehicle.attitude[pitch] diverged from its setpoint from t=2.229 to 10.278 s (peak |error| 34.645 deg)
effects.why: Pitch follows the pitch setpoint step, and throttle is 0 % over this stretch (cc_7), so energy loss may contribute.

outcomes.label: Raw GPS and compass steady, estimate jumps
outcomes.means: The estimator or fusion layer is at fault, and the setpoint swings follow from it.
outcomes.then: Inspect estimator innovations and sensor health.

outcomes.label: Raw sensors also jump
outcomes.means: The sensor inputs are faulty, or a real manoeuvre occurred.
outcomes.then: Inspect GPS and compass hardware and mounting.

outcomes.label: Raw and estimate steady, setpoint swings anyway
outcomes.means: The guidance or mission layer is commanding the swings.
outcomes.then: Review mission, mode and guidance parameters.

unknowns: Whether the vehicle was commanded into ±44 deg roll swings or guidance reacted to bad state estimates.
Whether the low-voltage warning mattered, because no voltage trace is in the recording.
Which flight mode was active, because only one event is recorded.

data_requests.what: Battery voltage and current, GPS raw, estimator status and flight mode
data_requests.why_needed: Separates the power, estimator and guidance hypotheses.

hypotheses.claim: Abrupt ±44 deg roll setpoint swings from guidance or mission logic caused the large attitude excursions.
hypotheses.because: The roll setpoint steps by 86.93 deg (line 45) while the inner loop follows at 0.975 correlation.

hypotheses.claim: Velocity and yaw estimates jump discontinuously, possibly from GPS or compass glitches feeding guidance.
hypotheses.because: Velocity[x] steps by -29.39 m/s at 13.001 s and yaw by -113.131 deg at 12.479 s, with no airspeed counterpart.

hypotheses.claim: A servo or an attitude sensor fault limits tracking.
hypotheses.because: Roll follows the setpoint at a stable 0.981 s lag and the typical difference falls to 3.191 deg in 30-60 s.

hypotheses.claim: Low battery or 0 % throttle from about 1 s to 13 s degraded pitch and altitude control.
hypotheses.because: The low-voltage warning at 0.518 s and zero throttle coincide with pitch divergence and a 15.747 m altitude step.

events.what: Battery low voltage warning at 0.518 s
events.why: Early warning with no recorded effect; the voltage trace is missing.
